newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat drops further on options-related sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat drops further on options-related sales.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures fell further at midsession on options-related selling which exacerbated the early slide triggered by USDA's 1996-97 wheat carryout number in USDA's May supply/demand report, traders said.
"There's selling out of the options pit. We could hit stops at $4.01-1/2 (per bushe/July) and there's a gap to fill at $3.99 (July)," a trader said.
The session low for July as of 1100 CDT was $4.02-1/2.
Traders said the market was hit by USDA's supply/demand and crop reports released at 0730 CDT.
USDA said 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryout would total 465 million bushels, above trader expectations for roughly 450 million bushels.
"They increased the wheat ending stocks which tells us we're going to have lower wheat prices this year," the trader said.
At 1103 CDT, wheat was two to 11-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down nine at $3.96. July was down 10-3/4 at $4.03-1/4.
